# Command reference

Every command of the running app, as `penumbra-cli ctl <command>` or a control-channel request sends it (see [Control](../control.md)). `{a, b?}` lists the params, `?` marks optional ones.


## general

| command | |
|---|---|
| `ping` | Check that the control channel answers |

## audio

| command | |
|---|---|
| `audio.config` | Audio settings for this run: {enabled?} |
| `audio.devices` | The audio inputs of this machine: name, default, rate, channels, format |
| `audio.status` | Audio input streams (device, rate, channels, open, error, frames, glitches, peak per channel in dBFS) |

## blob_track

| command | |
|---|---|
| `blob_track.learn` | A tex.blob_track takes a frame as the background (the empty scene): {path, delay?} (seconds before it does, default 0) |

## calib

| command | |
|---|---|
| `calib.homography` | Homography from 4 or more point pairs (normalised DLT); {pairs: [[[x,y],[u,v]],...]} |
| `calib.project` | Pixels of world points through a calibrated camera (null behind it); {camera, points: [[x,y,z],...]} |
| `calib.solve` | Calibrate a projector from world and picture points; {pairs: [[[x,y,z],[u,v]],...], size: [w,h], initial?, options?} |

## chan

| command | |
|---|---|
| `chan.read` | Cook a chan node and read its channels (values now; {samples: true} for all); {path, output?, samples?} |

## comp

| command | |
|---|---|
| `comp.collapse` | Group side-by-side nodes into a new component, ports where wires cross; {paths, name?} |
| `comp.expand` | Dissolve a component, its nodes move up beside it; {path} |
| `comp.library` | Component files in the project's components/, the user's library and penumbra's own library |
| `comp.load` | Add a component from a file or a library (by name); one in a folder of its own copies that folder's files into the project's library/<name>/ first; {file, path?} |
| `comp.remove` | Take a component file out of the library (into its removed/ folder); {name, place?: project \| library} |
| `comp.save` | Write a component to a file (default: the library, <name>.comp.ron); {path, file?} |

## cook

| command | |
|---|---|
| `cook.meter` | Pass times of the last 8 s: last, smoothed (1 s lag), median, 1 % high, max, cook thread busy; {samples?: [seconds ago, ms] per pass} |
| `cook.play` | Run or stop the show clock; {playing?} (default true) |
| `cook.stats` | Cook pass timings since the last reset: passes, slowest pass, longest gap, late frames, stalls; {reset?} |
| `cook.status` | Show clock, last cook pass, watched nodes, thumbnail policy |
| `cook.thumbnails` | The editor's thumbnails, kept with the project (settings thumbnails and thumbnail_every; one undo step); {mode?: always \| when_free \| never, every?: cook passes between two thumbnail cooks of a node, 1 = every frame} |

## dmx

| command | |
|---|---|
| `dmx.config` | DMX output settings for this run: {enabled?, blackout?}; blackout sends zeros on every output |
| `dmx.ports` | The serial ports of this machine (name, USB ids, whether it is an FT232R like the Open DMX USB) |
| `dmx.status` | DMX outputs (target, writers, device, open, error, frames, rate asked and measured, timings in ms) and inputs (listen, readers, open, error, packets, universes with their sources) |

## edit

| command | |
|---|---|
| `edit.begin` | Claim editing for Claude (needs 3 s without user edits); {label?}, which names the history entry |
| `edit.end` | Give editing back to the user |
| `edit.status` | Who is editing |

## geo

| command | |
|---|---|
| `geo.info` | Cook a geo node and describe it: parts (id, name, triangles), bounds, counts; {path, output?} |

## gpu

| command | |
|---|---|
| `gpu.info` | GPU adapter, texture size limit, memory, errors raised so far, whether lost |
| `gpu.simulate_loss` | Test aid: end the GPU device as if the driver had lost it. The app then closes as after a real loss, and the next start opens paused; {confirm: true} |

## help

| command | |
|---|---|
| `help.open` | The documentation page (docs/penumbra.html) in the default browser, at the entry of a node kind, a command or a guide; {kind?, open?}. Answers with its file and URL; open: false, and headless runs, open nothing |

## history

| command | |
|---|---|
| `history.list` | Recent history entries; {limit?} |
| `history.redo` | Redo one history entry |
| `history.undo` | Undo one history entry |

## job

| command | |
|---|---|
| `job.cancel` | Stop the helper job going on (projector.match, projector.flatfield before their next picture; scan.blend between its steps). Nothing is applied; {} |
| `job.status` | How the helper jobs stand (scan.blend, projector.match, projector.flatfield, also when started from the Helpers window): the one running (command, step, progress 0 to 1, seconds) and the last of each command (ok, message, warnings, its whole reply); {} |

## keyboard

| command | |
|---|---|
| `keyboard.press` | Press a key as if typed in a penumbra window, for chan.keyboard_in: {key, down?}; without `down` a tap, `down: true` holds it until `down: false` |
| `keyboard.status` | Keys held now (and by which window), the key pressed last, presses so far |

## mesh_out

| command | |
|---|---|
| `mesh_out.status` | Mesh files: node, file, format, mode, written_seconds_ago, triangles, parts, copies, bytes, writing, error; {path?} |
| `mesh_out.write` | Write an out.mesh's input to its file now, in either mode; {path}; answers with the status once written, fails with the node's error |

## mouse

| command | |
|---|---|
| `mouse.fake` | Stand in for the mouse, for chan.mouse_in: {x?, y?, buttons?: [left, right, middle], wheel?: notches}; x and y in desktop pixels put a fake pointer in place of the real one, {real: true} brings the real one back; wheel turns it by that many notches (up positive) |
| `mouse.status` | The mouse pointer as chan.mouse_in sees it (desktop pixels, buttons, faked or real), the wheel so far, the displays' rectangles |

## ndi

| command | |
|---|---|
| `ndi.sources` | The NDI sources on the network, this process's out.ndi nodes included (name as `PC (Source)`, address), and the NDI runtime in use. The first call starts looking: `settling` is true while the list may still be filling |

## node

| command | |
|---|---|
| `node.batch` | Apply ops as one all-or-nothing batch; {ops: [{op, ...}], label?} |
| `node.bind` | Drive a param (or one component, /t.translate.0) with a channel; {param, from, channel?} |
| `node.connect` | Connect an output to an input; without input: the first of its kind, or the next free one of a run (a composite's layers); {from, output?, to, input?} |
| `node.copy` | Copy side-by-side nodes with everything inside them; returns the text; {paths} |
| `node.create` | Create a node; {path, kind, params?} |
| `node.cut` | Copy side-by-side nodes, then delete them (one undo step); {paths} |
| `node.delete` | Delete a node and everything inside it; {path} |
| `node.disconnect` | Clear an input; {to, input} |
| `node.info` | One node: params, connections, cook status; {path} |
| `node.kinds` | Node types with their params, inputs and outputs. With a param: its help (what it does, type, default, range, unit, what each choice does); {kind?, param?} |
| `node.list` | Nodes under a path; {path?, recursive?} |
| `node.lock` | Lock (hold outputs) or unlock a node; {path, locked?} |
| `node.paste` | Paste the nodes copied last (or `text`) into a component or the root; {into?, text?} |
| `node.place` | Move nodes in the editor; top left corner, graph units on their component's plane, one undo step. null leaves a node to the editor to place; {nodes: {path: [x, y]}} |
| `node.rename` | Rename a node; {path, name} |
| `node.replace` | Replace a node with one of another kind under the same name (one undo step). Keeps the params, wires and bindings that fit and lists what was not kept; {path, kind} |
| `node.reset` | Start stateful nodes over (feedback, cache, time machine, tracker, filter...). A component resets the stateful nodes inside; locked nodes keep their outputs; {paths} or {path} |
| `node.set` | Set params, null resets to the default; {path, params: {name: value}} |
| `node.snapshot` | Cook a tex node (or a geo node: its picture) and write its output as PNG (8-bit sRGB); {path, output?, file?} |
| `node.unbind` | Back to the param's stored value; {param} |
| `node.watch` | Cook a node every frame (or stop); {path, watch?} |

## osc

| command | |
|---|---|
| `osc.config` | OSC settings for this run: {enabled?, max_packet?, rate?, burst?, pattern_rate?, max_addresses?} |
| `osc.learn` | Bind a param to the next OSC address that arrives with a number (or key a chan.keyboard_in lists, or the 3D mouse's button or axis moved most while a chan.spacemouse_in exists); {param, timeout?, wait?} or {cancel: true} |
| `osc.send` | Send one OSC message; {host?, port, address, args?: [numbers, strings, booleans]} |
| `osc.status` | OSC listeners (port, bound, packets, drops, sources), senders, recent messages, params set by address, learn |

## output

| command | |
|---|---|
| `output.list` | Connected displays (ids for out.projector's display), open output windows, projectors, pacing |

## palette

| command | |
|---|---|
| `palette.list` | Every palette a palette param can name, in list order (the place a bound channel picks): the built-in set, then the project's own from palettes.txt; each with kind, source and hex colours |
| `palette.remove` | Remove one of the project's own palettes from palettes.txt: {name} |
| `palette.set` | Define or change one of the project's own palettes: {name, colours: "31aaa9 f8e0a4 ..." or ["#31aaa9", ...]}; written to palettes.txt beside project.ron, used at once by every node naming it |

## project

| command | |
|---|---|
| `project.demo` | Open the demo project, made afresh: changes, state and layout from before are gone |
| `project.example` | Open a shipped example from a fresh copy in the user's data folder (the shipped one stays as it is). Changes last until the example is opened again; project.save_as keeps them; {name} |
| `project.examples` | The examples shipped with penumbra, by name, and where they lie |
| `project.info` | Project directory, unsaved changes, file errors, nodes that did not load (broken), who is editing |
| `project.new` | Make an empty project in dir (created if missing, must hold no project.ron) and open it; {dir} |
| `project.open` | Close this project (state saved, changes written) and open the one in dir; {dir} |
| `project.recent` | Recently opened projects, newest first (the demo is not listed), and the open one |
| `project.save` | Write project.ron now, also over a file that failed to merge (copied to project.ron.bak first) |
| `project.save_as` | Copy the open project (its files and the latest state snapshot) into dir (new or empty) and open the copy, a project of its own; {dir} |
| `project.settings` | Project settings with their values and what they do; {set?: {name: value}}, null resets (one undo step) |

## projector

| command | |
|---|---|
| `projector.flatfield` | Measure with a camera how brightness and colour vary across each projector's picture (hot spot, a colour cast towards an edge), and the brighter black where projectors overlap. Writes per projector a gain map and a black lift (gain_NAME.png, black_NAME.png) and connects them to out.projector's gain and black inputs. Blocks for about 20 s per projector; {camera (tex.video_in path), projectors (out.projector paths), scans (one scan folder per projector, with cam_to_proj.exr and proj_to_cam.exr, relative to the project; they must fit the current setup), even? (all: brightness and colour, measured on a flat evenly coloured surface \| colour: the colour cast only, which a relief's shading does not change), levels? (drive levels per primary, 5), low? (lowest level, sRGB-encoded drive, 0.6), frames? (camera frames averaged per picture, 4), settle? (s, 0.5), timeout? (s, 5), degree? (of the smooth surface fitted over the projector, 3), trim? (share of samples the fit may ignore, the surface's own pattern, 0.25), floor? (share of the picture allowed to stay dimmer than the target, 0.02), cover? (share of a projector's brightest that counts as lit for the black, 0.1), blur? (of the black lift, projector px, 6), contrast? (projector contrast, black = white / contrast, where the camera cannot read the black), out? (folder in the project, flatfield), apply? (true: connect the maps, one undo step), pictures? (false: also keep the camera's pictures, 16-bit sRGB PNGs, in out/pictures), wait? (false: start and answer at once; job.status follows it; true)} |
| `projector.match` | Measure the projectors with a camera (each alone: black, white, red, green and blue ramps) and write their colour correction (matrix, curves) so they look alike. Blocks for about half a minute per projector; {camera (tex.video_in path), projectors? (paths, default every active out.projector), levels? (8), settle? (s, 0.5), samples? (curve samples, 17), area? ([x, y, w, h] of the camera picture, 0..1), timeout? (s, 5), target? (reference: the others respond like the reference projector, the reference keeps straight curves, works through any camera \| srgb: every projector follows the sRGB curve, only with a camera known to be linear), refine? (rounds of closed-loop correction against the reference, the matrix on white, then the curves on greys; 5; 0 off), grey_levels? (greys the curves are refined on, evenly spaced; 3), save? (folder, relative to the project: also measures a grey ramp and writes each projector's measurement as NAME.json with NAME the node name, to match from later), note? (text saved with them: settings, lamp hours), apply? (true: write the params as one undo step), wait? (false: start and answer at once; job.status follows it and keeps the reply; true)}. Without the camera: {from (folder of NAME.json, or {projector path: file}), projectors?, samples?, apply?, wait?} matches from stored measurements; each camera channel follows the projector dimmest there, so the common white lies between the white points when no projector is the dimmest in every channel |
| `projector.test` | Switch the test pattern of every out.projector at once (its `test` and `test_pattern` params, one undo step): {on (true: the pattern instead of the input, false: the input again), pattern? (align: cells, centre cross, circle and edge, for keystone and alignment \| focus: one-pixel checkers and lines at the corners and the centre \| motion: bars and a frame strip moving on each presented frame, with the frame and late counts, for stutter and dropped frames after the GPU \| fields: full white, red, green, blue, black, projectors in turn, for dead pixels; unchanged when left out), projectors? (paths, default all)}. One projector showing a pattern draws it white; several draw in colours that keep overlapping ones apart |

## render

| command | |
|---|---|
| `render.frame` | Move the view.camera wired into a tex.render so its geometry fills the picture; the direction stays (orthographic: sets its size); {path} |

## res

| command | |
|---|---|
| `res.analyze` | What the projectors need of every node they show: size, needed, verdict, suggestion. Waits up to 3 s for render nodes to measure (pending: those that did not) |
| `res.optimize` | Give the nodes the suggested sizes, one undoable entry; {paths?, dry_run?} (paths: only these) |
| `res.overlay` | Colour the mappers' and render nodes' pictures by resolution (green 1:1, red coarse, blue wasted); {on?} |

## scan

| command | |
|---|---|
| `scan.align` | Line projectors in a row or a column up from their scans (folders scan.capture or scan.decode wrote). Fits a homography camera -> projector per scan; the content is the camera-axis rectangle spanning all their frames. Writes per projector its mapper's region (its share of the content) and corners (where that share lands in the projector), fit stretch, as one undo step; {scans: [folder, ...], mappers? ([tex.mapper path, ...], one per scan; without them only the report), apply? (true; false: report only)} |
| `scan.blend` | Blend weights for projectors lighting the same surface, from their scans (folders scan.decode wrote). Writes weight_N.png (16-bit, sRGB-encoded so tex.image_file gives the weight; multiply the projector's picture by it), detail_N.png (1 where this projector is the sharpest of those lighting a spot, for tex.blend_weight's detail mode) and proj_to_cam_smooth_N.exr (the map smoothed, for tex.remap); {scans: [folder, ...], masks? ([file or null, ...], e.g. scan.objects' labels_N.png), out? (folder, objects), ramp? (projector px, 200), blur? (projector px, 3), reach? (camera px, 6), sigma? (projector px, 6), into_scans? (write weight.png, detail.png and proj_to_cam_smooth.exr into each scan's folder, where tex.scan reads them, false), wait? (false: start and answer at once, job.status follows it; true)} |
| `scan.cancel` | Stop the scan going on (scan.run) before its next picture. The projectors show their pictures again; the files of earlier scans stay; {} |
| `scan.capture` | Scan projectors with a camera, live. Each projector alone shows the structured light patterns (in its own pixels, past its colour correction, the network untouched) while the others show black. The camera's frames are decoded and written as scan.decode writes them, into out/<projector> (the path without its leading slash, slashes as _). Measures the light-to-camera latency on the way. Blocks about 15 s per projector; {camera (tex.video_in path), projectors? (paths, default every active out.projector), out? (folder, scan), settle? (s after the latency, 0.05), timeout? (s, 5), level? (signal of the lit stripes, 1), levels? (instead of level: a scan per level, e.g. [1, 0.4], merged per camera pixel, the surest decode winning, so the dim pass decodes where the bright one clips; the first level's colour; 1 to 4 levels), frames? (keep the camera frames as PNG in out/<projector>/frames, frames_1, ... per level, false), verify? (take a picture only when two frames agree, true), retries? (frames that may disagree, 3), fill? (projector px, 32), options?: {min_contrast?, saturation?, min_confidence?, tolerance?, window? (camera px round a pixel over which the bits it resolves are judged, 7; 0 the whole picture), epipolar? (px a decoded pixel may lie off the geometry the decode as a whole obeys, else it is dropped: light thrown on by the walls decodes wrong, 4; 0 off)}} |
| `scan.decode` | Decode a structured light scan from the camera's pictures of tex.scan_pattern 0, 1, 2, ... (files in a folder, sorted by name, numbers by value). Writes cam_to_proj.exr and proj_to_cam.exr (maps for tex.remap), scene.png (the scene as the projector sees it) and quality.png; {frames (folder, relative to the project; or a list of folders: scans of one projector at different levels of light, merged per camera pixel, the surest decode winning, the first's colour), projector?: [w, h] (1920, 1080), out? (folder, default frames/decoded), fill? (projector px, 32), options?: {min_contrast?, saturation?, min_confidence?, tolerance?, window? (camera px round a pixel over which the bits it resolves are judged, 7; 0 the whole picture), epipolar? (px a decoded pixel may lie off the geometry the decode as a whole obeys, else it is dropped: light thrown on by the walls decodes wrong, 4; 0 off)}} |
| `scan.folders` | The scans in the project, what scan.blend and projector.flatfield take as scans: every folder (up to 4 deep, not state or library) holding cam_to_proj.exr and proj_to_cam.exr, with the out.projector it belongs to (the one a tex.scan writing it names, else the one it is named after), the tex.scan, whether scan.blend wrote its weight into it, and when its map was written (unix seconds); {} |
| `scan.objects` | Find the objects in front of a surface by parallax, per projector, between a scan of the empty scene (reference) and a scan with the objects (folders scan.decode wrote). The objects are numbered alike in every projector, top of the camera picture first. Writes per projector labels_N.png (8-bit, 0 background, k the object) and parts_N.png, plus objects_camera.png (the same labels in camera space, for shapes.trace with labels) and objects_camera_view.png; {projectors: [{reference, scan}, ...], out? (folder, objects), threshold? (camera px, 25), split? (camera px per projector px, 2), min_area? (projector px, 1/256 of the projector), erode? (projector px, 2), unmeasured? (projector px, 4), rim? (projector px, 25)} |
| `scan.patterns` | The pictures of a structured light scan in the order tex.scan_pattern shows them; {projector?: [w, h] (1920, 1080)} |
| `scan.regions` | The faces scan.scene found grouped into regions, one per part of the scene content treats as one (a crate's front with its rib strips and rims, a lid, a side), cleaned up (seams between a region's faces closed, holes filled, the ragged edge smoothed, four straight edges where the region is a quadrilateral, else straight borders where a line fits, as in scan.scene) and the floor switched off. The grouping is a list of regions, each a set of seed pixels in the camera picture (the face under each seed, or the nearest one within reach, belongs to it), an optional name and an optional enabled flag; faces under no seed are regions of their own; a region is enabled unless it says otherwise or lies mostly on the floor (found from the faces' planes against the support). It is kept in a file (regions.json in the scene folder) that `regions` replaces and `edit` changes: [{op: merge, at: [[x, y], ...], name?} (the faces under the points, and the regions they are in, become one region), {op: split, at: [x, y]} (the face under it leaves its region), {op: disable \| enable \| auto, at} (its region off, on, or back to the default), {op: name, at, name}, {op: clear}]. Writes regions_camera.png and regions_N.png per projector (8-bit, 0 none or disabled, enabled regions numbered top of the camera picture first; drop-in replacements for planes_camera.png and planes_N.png), regions_view.png (regions in colour, disabled faces striped grey, seeds as dots) and regions_reply.json (the reply: per region its faces, seeds, kind floor/level/upright, size, straight corners and per projector its plane; the faces with a pixel inside each to address them by; suggestions: thin faces lying on the plane of a large one they touch, rib strips next to their panel). {scene? (folder scan.scene wrote, scene), file? (the grouping, scene/regions.json), regions? ([{name?, seeds: [[x, y], ...], enabled?}, ...], replaces the file's), edit? ([op, ...], applied to the file's), out? (folder, the scene folder), seam? (camera px, 10), smooth? (camera px, 2.5), straight? (true), reach? (camera px, 12)} |
| `scan.relief` | Height maps of a mostly flat object (a relief panel) from its scans (folders scan.capture or scan.decode wrote), no reference scan needed. Per projector: a robust plane projector -> camera, the residual along its main direction as the height, the panel cut out at jumps, holes filled. Every projector is brought to the first one's units over the camera pixels both light (symmetric fit). Writes height_N.exr (0 to 1 over the heights' 1st to 99.5th percentile, for tex.lookup), mask_N.png (the light mask, for tex.image_file or scan.blend's masks), height_camera.exr and relief_view.png (the same in camera space, to look at); {scans: [folder, ...], out? (folder, relief), sign? ("auto" \| 1 \| -1: the first projector's sign, the others follow it by the overlap; auto is a heuristic, the wall around the panel taken as behind it; 1 and -1 are fixed to the camera's axes; the reply's sign.as_param pins what a run found), scale? ("symmetric" \| "least_squares"), jump? (camera px per projector px, 4), erode? (projector px, 4), reach? (projector px, 60: notches in the measured panel's outline up to twice this wide are lit, nothing past it)} |
| `scan.run` | The scan button of tex.scan nodes. Scans their projectors one after another with their camera (scan.capture, each into the node's folder), lines them up if every node names its mapper (scan.align, one undo step) and writes blend weights and smoothed maps into the scan folders (scan.blend); the nodes then show them. Runs in the background (scan.status, scan.cancel); {nodes? (tex.scan paths, default every tex.scan; all must name the same camera), wait? (return when done, with the report, false)} |
| `scan.scene` | Flat faces and the objects among them from one scan per projector (folders scan.capture or scan.decode wrote), no reference scan needed: every flat face (floor, wall, each face of each box) fits a homography of its own; they are found one fit after the other by RANSAC until no fit holds a face of min_plane, coplanar faces that do not touch (the tops of two boxes side by side) split into faces of their own, patches of curved surfaces dropped. What fits no face is an object; the face right below the objects is the support. Any face that is a rectangle of known aspect can be rectified: its four edges in the camera picture, completed where hidden, give the homography to its u and v. Borders between faces are straight where the measured one is a line (two faces meeting at a crease on the line their planes cross in, where every projector agrees and the measured border lies on it; else a fitted line with corners); where no line fits (curved or ragged borders) and along objects they stay as measured. Writes per projector planes_N.png and labels_N.png (8-bit, 0 none, k the face or object, numbered alike in every projector; labels_N.png as scan.objects writes it), scene_N.png (faces in colour, objects white), uv_K_N.exr per rectified face K (red and green its u along the outline's first edge and v along its last, 0 to 1; blue 1 on the face, also where nothing was measured, 0.5 on an object, 0.25 on another face; -1 outside the outline), height_N.exr and mask_N.png (the objects' height over the support, as scan.relief writes them); in camera space planes_camera.png, objects_camera.png, uv_K_camera.exr, height_camera.exr and scene_view.png (with the rectified faces' outlines and a grid in true squares); scene.json (the reply). {scans: [folder, ...], out? (folder, scene), rectify? ([{plane?, aspect: [width, depth], corners? ([[x, y] x 4] camera px, instead of finding them; without plane they give the face: the plane most pixels inside lie on, taken from the faces and objects it was split into, also where it sags a little)}, ...], else the support at 60:40), support? (plane number, or "rectified" for the first face in rectify; else the one below the objects), sign?, scale? (as scan.relief), tolerance? (camera px a pixel may lie off its face, 2), min_plane? (share of the measured pixels, 0.002), max_planes? (most faces kept, 255), min_object? (projector px, 1/256 of the projector), erode? (projector px the light mask shrinks, 2), straight? (straight borders in planes_camera.png and planes_N.png, true; planes_camera_measured.png keeps the measured ones), straight_tolerance? (camera px nine tenths of a measured border may lie off its line, 2), straight_length? (shortest straight border, px, 16)} |
| `scan.status` | How the scans of the tex.scan nodes stand: running, progress (0 to 1), step, the last run's error and warnings; {} |
| `scan.synthetic` | Writes the scans of a made-up room, ray cast, as scan.decode writes real ones: for trying scan.scene and the content after it without projectors or a camera. The room "pumpkin" is a landscape of five Euro crates with a ribbed pumpkin on one of them, two projectors left and right of the camera, decode noise like a real scan's; "landscape" three crates and a ball, "crate" one crate and a ball (both small and nearly noise free, as the tests use them). Writes per projector a folder (a, b) with proj_to_cam.exr, cam_to_proj.exr, scene.png and quality.png, and photo.png (the camera's picture of the room lit white by that projector, which a real decode does not write). {room? (pumpkin, landscape or crate; pumpkin), out? (folder, synthetic), scale? (pumpkin: camera and projectors are scale times 480 x 270 pixels, 0.25 to 8; 4, full HD), noise? (camera px, the standard deviation of the decode noise per axis; pumpkin 0.15 times scale), outliers? (share of pixels decoded far off, 0 to 0.1; pumpkin 0.002)} |

Replaces the lines of that tag; {path, from (node: path or name beside path), output?, tag? (trace), channel? (auto \| red \| green \| blue \| alpha \| luma), threshold? (0.5), invert? (inside is below it), labels? (every value its own shape), tolerance? (px, 1), min_area? (px, 64), append?, live? ## show

| command | |
|---|---|
| `show.lock` | Show mode on: the project is locked against edits and moves, not written and not reloaded from disk; OSC, DMX and the control channel stay live; after a crash (exit code 3) the app starts again with the clock running. Kept across restarts |
| `show.status` | Whether show mode is on, since when, the project it locks, restarts after crashes in the last 10 minutes |
| `show.unlock` | Show mode off: editing, saving and reloading as usual |

## state

| command | |
|---|---|
| `state.config` | Snapshot timing (not stored, every start has the defaults); {interval?, restore_on_start?}. Whether node state is kept at all is the project setting persist_state |
| `state.discard` | Discard what feedback loops, caches and other nodes hold, now and in the state files (locked nodes keep theirs) |
| `state.info` | Persistent state: settings, the files in the project's state directory, the last save and restore, what a snapshot would keep now |
| `state.restore` | Give the nodes their saved state back (latest, else previous, or {file}); replaces what they hold |
| `state.save` | Take a state snapshot now and wait for the file; {timeout?} in seconds |

## system

| command | |
|---|---|
| `system.check` | Show-machine settings that can ruin a show (gaming overlay, notifications) |
| `system.fix` | Apply one check's fix; replies with what it replaced; {id} |
| `system.load` | CPU over all cores and the busiest GPU engine in percent, sampled once a second while asked for (the first call waits for a sample). On NVIDIA GPUs `nvidia`: power_w, power_limit_w, temperature_c, clock_mhz, limited_by of the GPU penumbra renders on (`matched`), else the first |
| `system.process` | This process: working set, private bytes, handles, threads; GPU memory through wgpu's allocator |
| `system.restore` | Write back what system.fix replaced; {previous} as system.fix returned it |

## ui

| command | |
|---|---|
| `ui.arrange` | Arrange the nodes so wires cross little and run straight (one undo step): {nodes?: [path]}, else every level |
| `ui.camera` | The viewer's 3D view of a render or geometry: {mode?: picture\|free\|steer, home?, camera?: {eye, target, roll, fov, ortho?}, orbit?: [yaw, pitch], pan?: [right, up], dolly?, travel?: [right, up, forward], look?: [yaw, pitch], roll?, take?}; moves go to the free view's camera, in steer mode to the camera node (orthographic: dolly scales the view's size); take copies the free view into the camera node |
| `ui.click` | Click an element or a point; {id \| x, y, button?, double?, ctrl?, shift?, alt?} |
| `ui.drag` | Drag between elements or points; {from: {id \| x, y}, to: {id \| x, y}, button?, steps?} |
| `ui.elements` | Automation ids with rects in points; {prefix?} |
| `ui.enter` | Show the inside of a component in the editor, the top level without a path; {path?} |
| `ui.frame` | Fit all nodes into the editor |
| `ui.key` | Press a key (egui name: Delete, Tab, F, Z, Enter, ...); {key, ctrl?, shift?, alt?} |
| `ui.measure` | How tidy the level shown is, in graph units: width and height of the nodes, total and longest wire length, crossings, wire length on top of a wire from another output (overlap; where: overlaps), wire length through nodes |
| `ui.options` | The editor's options (right-click on empty space) and the viewer's channel options; {chan_bars?, viewer_background?, binding_lines?, chan_scale?: auto\|shared\|per_channel (auto: a lane per channel when one that moves would be flat on a shared scale), audio_view?: meters\|plot (what the viewer shows of a chan.audio_analysis: meters, beat and spectrum, or the channel plot), viewer_aspect?: auto\|number (width over height of the viewer's picture area; the height follows the column's width; dragging the viewer's edge sets the aspect, auto is 16:9)} |
| `ui.screenshot` | PNG of the window; {file?} (default %TEMP%/penumbra/ui.png) |
| `ui.scroll` | Mouse wheel over an element or point; {id \| x, y, dy} |
| `ui.select` | Select nodes in the editor (the editor shows the component they sit in); {paths} |
| `ui.state` | Selection, viewer, pan and zoom, editing mode, the status bar's message; {positions?} |
| `ui.type` | Type text into the focused field; {text} |
| `ui.view` | Pin the viewer to a node, or unpin without a path; {path?, output?: name or index} |
| `ui.window` | Where the editor window is, and moves it: {position?: [x, y], size?: [width, height], maximized?}; physical pixels of the desktop as output.list gives the displays, the position its outer top left corner, the size the part inside the frame; the window opens there again on the next start |
